articles.title: All the important news from the ongoing India AI Impact Summit
articles.summary: India is hosting a four-day AI Summit this week that will be attended by executives from major AI labs and Big Tech, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, Microsoft, Google, and Cloudflare, as well as heads of state.

articles.title: As AI data centers hit power limits, Peak XV backs Indian startup C2i to fix the bottleneck
articles.summary: C2i has raised $15 million as it tests a grid-to-GPU approach to reducing power losses in AI data centers.

articles.title: Blackstone backs Neysa in up to $1.2B financing as India pushes to build domestic AI infrastructure
articles.summary: Neysa is targeting deployments of more than 20,000 GPUs over time as demand for local AI compute accelerates.

articles.title: OpenClaw creator Peter Steinberger joins OpenAI
articles.summary: OpenAI said OpenClaw will live on as an open source project.

articles.title: Longtime NPR host David Greene sues Google over NotebookLM voice
articles.summary: The longtime host of NPR’s “Morning Edition,” is suing Google, alleging that the male podcast voice in the company’s NotebookLM tool is based on him.

articles.title: Anthropic and the Pentagon are reportedly arguing over Claude usage
articles.summary: The apparent issue: whether Claude can be used for mass domestic surveillance and autonomous weapons.

articles.title: India has 100M weekly active ChatGPT users, Sam Altman says

articles.title: The enterprise AI land grab is on. Glean is building the layer beneath the interface.
articles.summary: In this week's episode of the Equity podcast, Glean CEO Arvind Jain explains the company's shift from enterprise search tool to middleware layer for enterprise AI.

articles.title: Hollywood isn’t happy about the new Seedance 2.0 video generator
articles.summary: Hollywood organizations are pushing back against a new AI video model called Seedance 2.0, which they say has quickly become a tool for “blatant” copyright infringement.

articles.title: The great computer science exodus (and where students are going instead)

articles.title: Airbnb says a third of its customer support is now handled by AI in the US and Canada
articles.summary: Airbnb was poised to introduce an app that doesn't just search for you, but one that "knows you." CEO Brian Chesky said, "It will help guests plan their entire trip, help hosts better run their businesses, and help the company operate more efficiently at scale."

articles.title: Elon Musk suggests spate of xAI exits have been push, not pull
articles.summary: At least nine engineers, including two co-founders, have announced their exits from xAI in the past week, fueling online speculation and raising questions about stability at Musk’s AI company amid mounting controversy.

articles.title: Cohere’s $240M year sets stage for IPO
articles.summary: Cohere surpassed $240 million in annual recurring revenue in 2025, highlighting strong enterprise AI demand as the Canadian startup positions itself for a potential IPO amid intensifying competition from OpenAI and Anthropic.

articles.title: CISA seeks critical infrastructure sector input on cyber-incident reporting rule
articles.summary: CISA announced a series of town hall meetings with affected industries about the pending rule. The one for the energy and nuclear sectors is scheduled for March 9.

articles.title: Treasury issues FEOC guidance, clarifies material assistance cost ratio
articles.summary: The notice offers interim safe harbor guidance for calculating a project or component’s material assistance cost ratio, or MACR, and provides relevant MACR thresholds.

articles.title: The rate case for grid resilience: Why climate change isn’t just about storms
articles.summary: Utilities that delay resilience investments hoping that global climate mitigation efforts will reduce the need for local hardening are taking a dangerous gamble, writes Kai Karlstrom, director of solutions engineering at Repath.

articles.title: Transmission drives Exelon’s capital spending plan to $41.3B
articles.summary: Exelon has a “line of sight” on $12 billion to $17 billion of transmission buildout over the next 10 years that isn’t included in its current capital plan, a company official said.

articles.title: AEP contracted large load pipeline doubles to 56 GW
articles.summary: American Electric Power’s data center pipeline in Texas surged to 36 GW by the end of December, from 13 GW in the third quarter.

articles.title: Data centers pursue on-site power as affordability tops utility concerns: BofA
articles.summary: Hyperscalers are looking to secure power fast, “firm and smooth with storage, then layer in solar as the lowest-cost marginal energy,” wrote Bank of America Securities analyst Dimple Gosai.

articles.title: DOE ‘does not have a plan’ for oversight of billions in energy funds: GAO
articles.summary: Since the IIJA appropriated about $21.5 billion of “no-year appropriations” for clean energy demonstration projects, DOE will “have an ongoing need to solicit and review applications for additional projects,” the U.S. Government Accountability Office said.

articles.title: Minnesota’s distributed capacity procurement decision could shape the grid far beyond its borders
articles.summary: The Minnesota Public Utilities Commission should approve a framework that supports open, competitive participation, writes Coalition for Community Solar Access CEO Jeff Cramer.

articles.title: 300-MW Ameren fast-track project hits snag on DOE transmission funding uncertainty
articles.summary: It’s unclear if the U.S. Department of Energy will help fund a set of 345-kV projects in the Great Plains region, leaving Ameren Missouri in doubt about potential interconnection costs for its project.

articles.title: TVA board, remade by Trump, votes to keep coal plants open
articles.summary: There has been a “significant change in the regulatory outlook, particularly for coal, and that creates both the opportunity and the need for us to revisit these decisions,” said TVA CFO Tom Rice.

articles.title: ČEZ outlines USD392 million plant modernisation plans
articles.summary: Czech nuclear power operator ČEZ has set out its modernisation and investment plans for 2026 at the Dukovany and Temelin nuclear power plants.

articles.title: Yokogawa to supply Rolls-Royce SMR control systems
articles.summary: Japanese industrial automation specialist Yokogawa Electric Corporation is to provide the data processing and control systems for the initial Rolls-Royce SMR small modular reactor units.

articles.title: Darlington refurb completed ahead of schedule, under budget
articles.summary: The refurbishment of the fourth and final Candu reactor at the Darlington nuclear power plant in Ontario has been completed and the unit is expected to be restarted later this month, four months ahead of schedule.

articles.title: Lianjiang simulator completes on-site acceptance testing
articles.summary: The full-scope simulator for Phase I of the Lianjiang nuclear power plant - comprising two CAP1000 reactors - in China's Guangdong province has passed acceptance tests after having been installed on-site.

articles.title: Deep Isolation launches full-scale demonstration programme
articles.summary: US nuclear waste disposal company Deep Isolation has announced the launch of its multi-year, full-scale, at-depth deep borehole demonstration programme to test its technology for safely and permanently disposing of nuclear waste deep underground.

articles.title: WANO rolls out new enhanced monitoring initiative
articles.summary: The World Association of Nuclear Operators has launched its Enhanced Performance Monitoring system for all 400+ of its member nuclear energy units, providing continuous monitoring of plant performance.

articles.title: US, Japanese partnership for fusion technology development
articles.summary: The US Department of Energy and private Japanese fusion technology company Kyoto Fusioneering have established a landmark partnership to deliver critical fusion infrastructure and perform collaborative R&D to drive down technology and commercialisation risk.

articles.title: Location of second Kazakh nuclear power plant announced
articles.summary: Kazakhstan's second nuclear power plant will be constructed in the Zhambyl district of the Almaty region - adjacent to the site selected for the country's first nuclear plant - the government has decided.

articles.title: Materials successfully tested for HTGR, says Rosatom
articles.summary: Structural components made of a carbon-carbon composite material designed for a high-temperature gas-cooled reactor have passed tests at temperatures of up to 1300 degrees Celsius, Rosatom says.

articles.title: First unit at China's Taipingling plant starts up
articles.summary: Unit 1 at the Taipingling nuclear power plant has attained a sustained chain reaction for the first time, China General Nuclear announced. The unit is the first of six Hualong One (HPR1000) reactors planned for the site in Guangdong province.

articles.title: UK seeking pipeline of advanced nuclear projects
articles.summary: The UK government has published a first-of-its-kind framework that aims to stimulate private investment in innovative nuclear technologies – including advanced, small, and micro modular reactors – across the country, providing a clear route to market and support for credible projects to get them off the ground.

articles.title: US to exclude advanced nuclear from NEPA environmental process
articles.summary: The Department of Energy has announced a "categorical exclusion for authorisation, siting, construction, operation, reauthorisation, and decommissioning of advanced nuclear reactors for inclusion in its National Environmental Policy Act implementing procedures".

articles.title: Natura, NGL collaboration on water treatment
articles.summary: US liquid-fueled molten salt reactor developer Natura Resources has partnered with energy and water infrastructure company NGL Energy Partners LP to examine combining Natura's advanced nuclear reactor technology with thermal desalination for power production and oil and gas produced water treatment.

articles.title: Inner dome installed at Zhangzhou 3
articles.summary: The inner safety dome has been installed on the containment building of unit 3 of the Zhangzhou nuclear power plant in China's Fujian province, China National Nuclear Corporation announced. Zhangzhou 3 is the third of six Hualong One units planned for the site.

articles.title: First concrete poured for Hungary's Paks II nuclear project
articles.summary: A ceremony has been held to mark the start of construction of the reactor building's foundation for Hungary's Paks II nuclear power plant.

articles.title: New lease of life for US legacy nuclear sites
articles.summary: The US Department of Energy's Office of Environmental Management announced it is restarting uranium recovery operations at the Savannah River Site H Canyon facility in South Carolina and is partnering with nuclear fuel company General Matter for the potential use of the Fuels and Materials Examination Facility at the Hanford site in Washington Stat

articles.title: India extends existing tax waivers for nuclear to 2035
articles.summary: The Indian government's budget proposes "to extend the existing basic customs duty exemption on imports of goods required for Nuclear Power Projects till the year 2035 and expand it for all nuclear plants irrespective of their capacity".

articles.title: Sweden proposes steps to facilitate new nuclear projects
articles.summary: The Swedish government has announced several proposed measures to make it easier to establish new nuclear power in the country. These include a new approval law, more possible locations for nuclear power on the coast, and increased government support for municipalities' feasibility studies.

articles.title: US Nuclear Regulatory Commission launches reorganisation
articles.summary: The US nuclear regulator is aiming to implement a reorganisation which it says will streamline decision-making, consolidate functions, and align with national goals for more efficient licensing and deployment of nuclear technology by the end of September.

articles.title: TRISO fuel progress for US reactor pilot programme
articles.summary: BWX Technologies says its TRISO nuclear fuel for Antares Nuclear is on track for "timely completion" for the reactor demonstration planned to meet the US’s 4 July target date.
